capabilities.name: Event-driven single-instrument and multi-instrument cash portfolio backtesters
capabilities.evidence_status: Deterministic single-instrument event simulator plus separate multi-instrument, single-provider, long-only NSE cash portfolio simulator. Supports event ordering, source selection, order/cancel latency, time-in-force, partial fills, participation caps, cash/exposure reservations, fees, spread, taker impact and conservative L2 queue approximation. Passive queue advancement requires explicit trade event and known aggressor side. Not an exchange matching engine; queue/impact require calibration.

capabilities.name: Shared raw ingress port with Upstox and FYERS adapters
capabilities.evidence_status: Market-archive ingress module routes original Upstox V3 protobuf bytes and FYERS SDK-decoded callback JSON bytes, each with source-specific metadata, through the durable raw-frame journal. Source binding, duplicate/sequence/malformed accounting, disconnect stops and journal-rebuilt checkpoints are shared by both adapters. A journal replay source replays captured bytes through the same port with exact metadata fidelity and idempotent replay into a resumed journal. Seventeen dedicated tests cover replay-after-restart dedup, ordinal-fenced replay beyond the bounded hash window, post-commit continuity advancement, bounded continuity state and cross-source isolation; no provider decoding or canonical instrument resolution is performed here, and no live entitlement or network path is certified.

capabilities.name: Source-backed corporate financial facts and point-in-time validation
capabilities.evidence_status: Initial pure Rust domain and bounded JSONL validation CLI added. Exact decimal facts, company identity observations, source document hashes and locators, append-only fact revisions, derived-input lineage, and point-in-time selection are implemented with unit/integration fixtures. Targeted Rust compilation, tests, Clippy, and hosted CI are pending; no MCA/SEBI/NSE/BSE network adapter, PDF/XBRL parser, production store, source entitlement, or complete-company coverage is claimed.

capabilities.name: Verified offline FYERS session importer
capabilities.evidence_status: The fyers-importer binary verifies the Python SDK session manifest and full hash chain, validates every record, preserves event and gap metadata through canonical re-encoding, and imports idempotently into the shared raw journal through DurableIngestor. Three tests use a fixture generated by the real Python hash-chain journal. No live IPC, entitlement verification or canonical event projection is performed.

capabilities.name: Version-bound canonical event projection (Upstox and FYERS)
capabilities.evidence_status: quantlab normalize binds both Upstox decoded frames and FYERS SDK callback journals to an exact reference revision, records normalizer and event-schema versions, requires source_frame_sha256 for archived observations, leaves unknown instruments unresolved, and replays byte-identically in a fresh process. Seven projection tests cover these properties; no competing Rust event model or live path is introduced.

capabilities.name: Deterministic paper consumption of canonical projections
capabilities.evidence_status: quantlab paper-replay consumes canonical events with explicit provider selection, refuses unresolved instruments and missing source-frame lineage, verifies an optional reference binding against the projection sidecar, and writes byte-identical results from fresh processes using a no-intent strategy. Five tests; no engine rewrite, live path or trading.

capabilities.name: Active challenge SBE decoder with protocol differential evidence
capabilities.evidence_status: crates/sbe-codec decodes challenge schema id 1 version 2 templates 1 and 2 with no predecessor type dependency. Four differential tests verify the frozen golden digest, reproduce the independent C++ SBE canonical dump byte for byte, assert byte-identical canonical re-encoding, and refuse the seven malformed cases. The oracle is the C++ SBE decoder only; the numeric/book oracle is not used as SBE evidence.

capabilities.name: Checked-in KDB-X analytics contract and deterministic golden harness
capabilities.evidence_status: analytics/kdb/mbp_metrics.q is a checked-in typed per-source MBP contract; apps/kdb-lab parses typed observations and metrics, runs a local KDB-X engine with absolute paths, records input/output digests, and pins behaviour with byte-identical synthetic golden files. Thirteen Rust tests cover contract shape, gap/unit invariants, reference arithmetic, report golden equality (schema validation via the contract gate) and real-engine replay; the golden replay is skipped where q is absent. The 2026-11-20 real Upstox run produced 36 rows and 87.07 s with 0 gaps. No broker, order or licensed session data is used; this is research analytics, not authoritative money arithmetic or a profitability claim.

capabilities.name: Tri-state source data-rights contract with evidence provenance
capabilities.evidence_status: The source-product registry records capture/store/replay/redistribute as UNKNOWN, PERMITTED or PROHIBITED with source, document reference, scope and review date; UNKNOWN never grants a right and store/replay requirements fail closed. A registry-level written-evidence review lists the seven required evidence classes. The Kite quote product now declares a snapshot, with cross-field schema rules enforcing snapshot/recovery/depth coherence. All rights remain UNKNOWN pending owner evidence; no entitlement or data right is claimed.

capabilities.name: Fail-closed risk authority startup
capabilities.evidence_status: A newly constructed RiskAuthority now has session closed, account snapshot unavailable, kill switch engaged and reconciliation blocked, so it denies new risk until readiness facts are supplied by their owners. Readiness control flags no longer bump the economic-state revision. A fresh-authority test asserts all four fail-closed checks; the synthetic paper runner supplies readiness explicitly and records that these values are fixtures, not measured evidence. This is the M3.6.0 prerequisite only, not complete health-to-risk integration.
